sources.quote: Osmosis is water movement through a semipermeable membrane, from an area of lesser solute concentration to an area of greater solute concentration, in an attempt to equalize the solute concentrations on either side of the membrane.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Only fluids and some particles dissolved in the fluid are able to pass through a semipermeable membrane; larger particles are blocked from getting through.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Because osmosis causes fluid to travel due to a concentration gradient and no energy is expended during the process, it is referred to as passive transport.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Protein content of the blood (in the form of albumin) causes oncotic pressure that holds water inside the vascular compartment.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Hydrostatic pressure opposes oncotic pressure at the arterial end of capillaries, where it pushes fluid and solutes out into the interstitial compartment.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: On the venous end of the capillary, hydrostatic pressure is reduced, which allows oncotic pressure to pull fluids and solutes back into the capillary.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Osmosis causes fluid movement between the intravascular, interstitial, and intracellular fluid compartments based on solute concentration.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: Due to the elevated solute concentration within the bloodstream, osmosis causes fluid to be pulled into the intravascular compartment from the interstitial and intracellular compartments to try to equalize the solute concentration.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement

sources.quote: As fluid leaves the cells, they shrink in size.
sources.section: 15.2 Basic Fluid and Electrolyte Concepts, Fluid Movement
